defect.description: Input_args given as ordinary ffmpeg arguments in a string rather than a preset name (for example '-rtsp_transport tcp') are concatenated as a str onto the argument list: get_ffmpeg_arg_list(...) + '-rtsp_transport tcp' raises TypeError (can only concatenate list to list), so audio detection fails to start; the fallbacks need get_ffmpeg_arg_list(...) like the global args.

review_items: src/audio.py:17 — plain-string ffmpeg_input.input_args falls through as a str, causing list+str TypeError
src/audio.py:20 — same issue on the camera-wide ffmpeg.input_args fallback; fix by wrapping fallbacks in get_ffmpeg_arg_list
votes.evidence_quote: When `ffmpeg_input.input_args` is a plain string of ffmpeg arguments (not a preset name), `parse_preset_input` returns `None`, so `or ffmpeg_input.input_args` evaluates to the raw `str`. Then `get_ffmpeg_arg_list(ffmpeg.global_args) + str` raises `TypeError: can only concatenate list (not "str") to list`.
votes.justification: The review identifies the exact defect in get_ffmpeg_command in src/audio.py: plain-string input_args fall through as a str and trigger a list+str TypeError. It also gives the same fix, wrapping the fallbacks in get_ffmpeg_arg_list. Both findings describe the same defect at two of its fallback sites.
